Tactical Map — Russia and the former Soviet states …
LAYERS
INFRASTRUCTURE
…
Map basis: Lambert conformal conic (standard parallels 45 and 75 degrees north; central meridian 100 degrees east), drawn from Natural Earth country boundaries and oblast, republic and province borders for Russia and the former USSR. The frame runs from 18 degrees east to 191.5 degrees east (Chukotka is drawn across the date line, so it joins the main territory) and from 34.5 to 82.5 degrees north. Russia and the 14 other former Soviet states are shaded; neighbouring countries are outlines. India is outside the frame and nothing about India is plotted. Disputed or occupied areas are described, not settled: Crimea and the occupied parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson (Ukrainian territory that Russia controls; most states do not recognise the annexation); Abkhazia and South Ossetia (Georgia disputes them); Transnistria (Moldova); the Kuril Islands (Japan claims them). Russian nuclear weapons storage sites are not publicly disclosed and are not plotted. Most positions are approximate; each tooltip gives its source and whether it is verified in this build. Strikes and claims are reported by one side or the other. Events reflect reports up to 10 October 2026.

Darkweb & Threat Intel…
Sources: Ransomware.live (leak-site claims - group claims, not verified facts); Telegram threat-intel channels; and dark-web RSS sources reached through Tor that you verify yourself (data/onion_sources.json).
To read onion sources you need Tor on this PC: open Tor Browser (it listens on port 9150) or install and start the Tor service (port 9050). Keep it running, then press Refresh. Nothing is needed for the clear-web and Telegram sources. This dashboard never opens .onion pages in a browser and does not search or crawl the dark web.
